title: Antenna reconstruction correctness validation campaign

status_vocabulary.solved/pass: A local HFSS reference was built, solved, and passed its stated reference gate. This does not imply that an independently generated candidate has passed.
status_vocabulary.candidate-solved/pass: Both the local reference and an independently generated candidate passed their contracts and same-version electromagnetic comparison gates.
status_vocabulary.solved/fail-paper-gate: A local HFSS translation was built and solved, but it did not reproduce the paper-explicit electromagnetic acceptance targets and therefore is not an accepted candidate reference.
status_vocabulary.static-tested/pending-solve: The benchmark contract and deterministic implementation pass offline checks, but no accepted HFSS reference curve has been solved yet.
status_vocabulary.static-tested/blocked: The benchmark contract and deterministic implementation pass offline checks, but no accepted HFSS reference curve exists because the solver license is unavailable.
status_vocabulary.queued: The source has been selected, but no frozen benchmark implementation or accepted HFSS result exists.

campaign_rules: Never describe an offline contract or import test as electromagnetic correctness evidence.
A license checkout failure is an execution blocker, not an antenna-model failure.
Paper-explicit values and cross-solver engineering assumptions must remain separately labelled.
A generated candidate is accepted only after both its contract and its independently solved S11 curve pass the applicable gates.
Use repository-relative artifact paths; do not depend on a specific project name, gRPC port, user directory, or job identifier.

cases.title: Official PyAEDT probe-fed patch
cases.status_scope: local HFSS reference and independent candidate passed G0-G5 including same-version S11 comparison

source.title: Probe-fed patch antenna - PyAEDT Examples
source.evidence: Official example construction and its documented parameters.

key_parameter_evidence: Copper ground and signal layers are each 0.035 mm thick; the Duroid substrate is 0.5 mm thick.
The rectangular patch is 9.57 mm by 9.25 mm and targets 10 GHz.
The probe relative x offset is 0.485; the terminal solution adapts at 10 GHz and sweeps 8-12 GHz.
The expanded official construction contains nine named model objects plus Radiation, Perfect E, and Wave Port boundaries.
uncertainties: The official web example currently targets a newer AEDT release than the local 2025.1 reference, so every candidate must be solved with the same local AEDT/PyAEDT versions as its comparison reference.
The official page does not publish a frozen numeric S11 CSV; the accepted curve is a locally generated reference.
The first independent project candidate attempt produced five structured artifacts but local qwen3-vl:8b timed out in model_3d after 900 seconds.

The first same-job DeepSeek text-stage retry generated through simulation_setup, but five component primitives drifted from source evidence, two Python stages returned nested build functions, geometry subtraction was duplicated, and the solver contract remained incomplete.

A second strict retry preserved the source primitives and immediate-fragment form, but eight contract fields still failed and the code used incompatible PyAEDT 0.26.3 calls, crossed stage responsibilities, repeated geometry/simulation operations, and left the coaxial port physics unresolved.

The latest fail-closed dimensions retry exposed a deeper upstream defect: source evidence omitted Stackup resize/fill-body semantics and used the wrong probe formula, so source_analysis must be regenerated before any AEDT execution.

The first source-only retry failed before artifact registration because JSON evidence was incorrectly routed to Ollama vision; MIME-aware text/visual routing is now fixed and the failed stage can resume directly.
The first resumed DeepSeek response used a non-array coordinate_system.axes value and was rejected before registration; the exact schema prompt is now integrated.

The next DeepSeek response fixed axes but used evidence instead of evidence_source, put prose in required_relationships, and marked the air-filled signal body as copper; it was retained as rejected source audit v001 and never registered or executed.

Frozen JSON benchmarks can now publish a generic source_contract that enforces component roles, primitive/material/fill/body semantics, parameters, relationships, and ordered operations before source acceptance; the official benchmark also includes Stackup3D's internal signal-minus-Patch keep-originals operation.

The next source response completed with the correct object, parameter, and operation sets, but manual review rejected prose-only geometric_evidence and a misleading ambiguity note before downstream use; structured component geometry is now mandatory and preserved into solids/dimensions.

The structured-geometry retry matched all nine components and fourteen operations but promoted percentage_offset_argument=0.25 into a thirteenth design parameter; the exact twelve-parameter contract rejected and versioned it, while preserving that implementation constant for derived relations.

The direct source-stage resume then passed with exactly nine components, twelve parameters, fourteen operations, X/Y/Z axes, and structured per-component geometry; this source is accepted for downstream offline generation but is not candidate HFSS or electromagnetic evidence.

The v006 dimensions candidate was numerically complete but initially rejected because the generic gate disallowed an explicitly null Region material and ignored the existing nested dimensions container; both validator defects are fixed, X/Y/Z preservation is enforced, and the immutable rejected v001 text passes read-only revalidation.

On 2026-08-26 the recovered independent candidate completed through simulation_setup, passed all static execution gates and 124/124 frozen contract checks, and was exported as immutable generated_model_v001.py.

The candidate was then built and solved with the same AEDT 2025.1/PyAEDT 0.26.3 environment as the reference; its adaptive solution converged at pass 11 and its G5 resonance, bandwidth, and curve-RMSE checks all passed.
acceptance_criteria: Reference contract, nine-object topology, required boundaries, adaptive frequency, and sweep must match the frozen benchmark.
The local reference must resonate within 1% of 10 GHz and reach S11 at or below -10 dB; this gate passed.
The independent candidate contract passed, and its same-version comparison passed resonance error <= 1%, bandwidth error <= 5%, and curve RMSE <= 1 dB.

Optimization variables must pass geometry-effect preflight, every eligible trial must converge at Delta S <= 0.02 with a converged sweep, and the source project hash must remain unchanged; all gates passed in the 12-trial regression.
cases.next_action: Preserve the G0-G5 and 12-trial optimization records as regression baselines; apply the same evidence and convergence gates only after each paper-derived design independently passes its reference and candidate gates.

cases.title: Yeo 2019 conventional inset-fed RF-35 patch
cases.status_scope: local baseline and three controlled HFSS variants solved; none reproduced the complete paper gate

source.title: Slot-Loaded Microstrip Patch Sensor Antenna for High-Sensitivity Permittivity Characterization
source.evidence: Figure 1(a), Figure 2, and Section 2, especially the explicit geometry on PDF page 4 and bandwidth/Q statements on page 5.

key_parameter_evidence: RF-35 substrate: relative permittivity 3.5, loss tangent 0.0018, thickness 0.76 mm; board/ground 80 mm by 80 mm.
Patch 40 mm by 31.9 mm; feed 1.66 mm by 24.5 mm; inset 2.8 mm by 9 mm.
Paper resonance 2.5 GHz; published VSWR < 2 / S11 < -10 dB interval 2.490-2.510 GHz; fractional bandwidth 0.8%; Q = 125.

recorded_controlled_assumption_study.held_fixed: all paper-explicit dimensions and RF-35 properties

uncertainties: The paper used CST; conductor material/thickness, feed-port construction, boundary clearance, mesh, convergence, and sweep settings are not published.
Copper at 0.035 mm, a 50-ohm HFSS wave port, coordinate placement, radiation padding, and solver settings are explicitly labelled engineering assumptions.
The black Figure 2 curve is overdrawn by the red curve at resonance and cannot provide a defensible numeric golden curve.
acceptance_criteria: All paper-explicit geometry/material fields and Figure 1(a) topology must match the benchmark; assumptions must not be relabelled as paper evidence.
A local HFSS reference must first reproduce a 2.5 GHz fundamental within 1% and show a -10 dB band consistent with the published 2.490-2.510 GHz interval.
After that paper gate passes, an independent candidate must pass its contract and same-version reference comparison with resonance error <= 1%, bandwidth error <= 10%, and curve RMSE <= 1.5 dB.

blocker.diagnostic: The baseline plus solid-lumped, PEC-wave, and PEC-lumped controlled variants were solved in AEDT 2025.1; no variant passed the complete resonance and first -10 dB band gate.
blocker.interpretation: The current HFSS translations are not accepted reference baselines. The mismatch may arise from unpublished CST port, conductor, boundary, mesh, or other implementation choices; paper-explicit dimensions must not be silently tuned.

cases.next_action: Keep the independent-candidate gates closed for this case, preserve the negative result, and continue reference validation with the scaled Yeo case while seeking stronger CST or implementation evidence.

cases.title: Yeo 2019 scaled radiating-edge-slot-loaded RF-35 patch
cases.status_scope: local baseline and three controlled HFSS variants solved; none reproduced the complete dual-mode paper gate

source.title: Slot-Loaded Microstrip Patch Sensor Antenna for High-Sensitivity Permittivity Characterization
source.evidence: Figure 1(c), Figure 2, and Section 2, especially the scaled geometry, resonances, bandwidth, and Q on PDF page 5.

key_parameter_evidence: Shared RF-35/board values: er 3.5, tan(delta) 0.0018, h 0.76 mm, and 80 mm by 80 mm ground.
Patch 31.8 mm by 25.4 mm; feed 1.66 mm by 27.3 mm; inset 2.3 mm by 12 mm.
Radiating-edge slot 1 mm by 29.8 mm, positioned 1 mm from the radiating edge.
Paper resonances 2.5 and 3.465 GHz; first -10 dB interval 2.496-2.503 GHz; fractional bandwidth 0.28%; Q = 357.

recorded_controlled_assumption_study.held_fixed: all paper-explicit dimensions, radiating-edge slot, and RF-35 properties

uncertainties: The paper used CST and omits conductor, port, boundary, mesh, convergence, and sweep implementation details.
The HFSS translation freezes those missing choices as labelled assumptions rather than inferred paper facts.
The 7 MHz first bandwidth spans about two source-image pixels; the red raster curve is broadened by its 3-5 pixel line width and is not a strict S11 golden curve.
The paper does not state the upper-mode -10 dB bandwidth.
acceptance_criteria: All paper-explicit geometry/material fields and Figure 1(c) slot topology must match without importing Figure 1(b) dimensions.
A local HFSS reference must first place both modes within 1% of 2.5 and 3.465 GHz and reproduce the narrow first published band as closely as documented assumptions permit.

After the paper gate passes, an independent candidate must pass its contract and same-version reference comparison with per-mode resonance error <= 1%, bandwidth error <= 10%, and curve RMSE <= 1.5 dB.
Raster-derived first-band width must not replace the explicit 2.496-2.503 GHz prose target.

blocker.diagnostic: The baseline plus solid-lumped, PEC-wave, and PEC-lumped controlled variants were solved in AEDT 2025.1; no variant reproduced both resonances and the published first narrow band.
blocker.interpretation: The current HFSS translations are not accepted reference baselines. Paper-explicit dimensions and slot topology must not be silently tuned.

cases.next_action: Keep the independent-candidate gates closed for this case, preserve the negative result, and continue with the 5.25 GHz Wi-Fi reference.

cases.title: El-Gendy 5.25 GHz single Wi-Fi patch element
cases.status_scope: source-corrected reference plus ten one-at-a-time and eleven interaction engineering-assumption variants solved and converged; all failed the complete 5.15-5.35 GHz paper band

source.title: Wi-Fi Access Point Design Concept Targeting Indoor Positioning for Smartphones and IoT
source.evidence: Section 3.1, Figure 2, Table 1, and Figure 3; only the single patch element is in scope.

key_parameter_evidence: FR-4: relative permittivity 4.5, loss tangent 0.025, thickness 1.5 mm.
Lg = 25.92 mm, Wg = WR = 34.44 mm, LR = 20 mm, Lp = 12.55 mm, Wp = 17.22 mm, and probe offset Xp = 2.89 mm.
The paper targets 5.25 GHz and reports S11 <= -10 dB across 5.15-5.35 GHz.

recorded_engineering_assumption_search.record_sha256_policy: Every trial freezes the assumption and paper-parameter hashes plus its S11 SHA-256.

uncertainties: The paper used CST and does not publish conductor material/thickness, SMA/coax dimensions, connector dielectric, boundary placement/type, mesh/convergence, sampling details, or numeric S11 samples.
The HFSS model therefore freezes zero-thickness PEC sheets, a coaxial probe/terminal port, its radii and feed length, radiation padding, coordinate mapping, and sweep as engineering assumptions.
The reflector interpretation follows Figure 2 but remains a cross-solver translation decision.
acceptance_criteria: The local HFSS reference must itself satisfy S11 <= -10 dB over the complete 5.15-5.35 GHz paper band before it can become the comparison baseline.
If that paper gate fails, change only a documented assumption and preserve every paper-explicit parameter.
After the reference gate passes, an independent candidate must pass the contract and same-version comparison with resonance error <= 1%, band-edge/bandwidth error <= 10%, and curve RMSE <= 1 dB.

blocker.diagnostic: The source-corrected design, ten one-at-a-time variants, and eleven interaction variants converged. The v2 best full-band worst point is -8.4920 dB rather than <= -10 dB.
blocker.interpretation: The tested HFSS translations are not accepted references. A deep resonance minimum cannot substitute for agreement over the complete published band.

cases.next_action: Keep candidate gates closed and preserve the frozen v2 negative evidence. Before any v3, obtain new source evidence or define a separately versioned engineering-assumption hypothesis; do not change paper-explicit dimensions or promote any result unless it passes the complete paper band.

cases.title: Kaur 2021 CPW-fed split-ring-slot UWB monopoles
cases.status_scope: all three isolated HFSS translations solved; baseline matching and both full notch-case gates failed

source.title: Split Ring Slot Loaded Compact CPW-Fed Printed Monopole Antennas for Ultra-Wideband Applications with Band Notch Characteristics
source.evidence: Section 2 and Table 1 define the UWB monopole; Figure 7 and Table 2 define the two SRS variants; the abstract and results state the operating/notch bands.

key_parameter_evidence: FR-4 board 18 mm by 18 mm, relative permittivity 4.4, loss tangent 0.02, and thickness 1.6 mm.
Table 1: WF = 1.2 mm, LF = 5.934 mm, WP = 13.5 mm, LP = 9 mm, WG = 7.95 mm, LG = 5.4 mm, X1 = 6 mm, and Y1 = 1.5 mm.
Table 2 WLAN SRS: R1 = 2.4 mm, R2 = 2.1 mm, S1 = 0.4 mm; X-band SRS: R1' = 2.1 mm, R2' = 1.6 mm, S1' = 0.4 mm.
Reported baseline UWB range is 3-12 GHz with VSWR <= 2; WLAN rejection is centred at 5.3 GHz over 5.15-5.81 GHz; X-band rejection is centred at 7.4 GHz over 7.16-7.71 GHz.
uncertainties: Figure 7 does not dimension the exact vertical patch placement, SRS centre, or split orientation; the frozen coordinate interpretation is labelled as an assumption.
Conductor material/thickness, CPW excitation geometry, open boundary, mesh, convergence, and frequency sampling are not published and remain labelled assumptions.
No numeric simulated or measured S-parameter data file is published; strict candidate RMSE requires a same-version local HFSS reference rather than the raster plot.
acceptance_criteria: Keep the baseline, WLAN SRS, and X-band SRS parameters in three separate contracts and preserve every paper-explicit dimension.
For the baseline, require VSWR <= 2 across 3-12 GHz.
For each SRS variant, require the full published rejection interval at VSWR >= 2, the surrounding UWB bands at VSWR <= 2, peak centre error <= 0.15 GHz, and simulated peak VSWR relative error <= 20%.
Only after a local reference passes the paper gate may a same-version S11 curve become the candidate-comparison baseline.

blocker.diagnostic: All three designs solved normally after the XZ-port correction. Baseline worst S11 is -1.2438 dB over 3-12 GHz; both notch cases fail surrounding matched bands and notch-centre/peak checks.
blocker.interpretation: None of the three curves is an accepted reference. Undimensioned Figure 7 placement and unpublished port, conductor, boundary, and CST choices remain unresolved.

cases.next_action: Keep all Kaur candidate gates closed, preserve the negative results, and use the official probe-patch case as the only current G0-G5 regression baseline.
